changeSet.comment: (1) nexus.catalog_collections.collection_id bigint GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY: the registry's surrogate key. The ADD COLUMN fills every existing row from the column's own sequence in the DDL (a small table, ordinary changeset work: 171 rows on nexus and 42 on gate-xr789 at the P3.2 census); BY DEFAULT and not ALWAYS so a writer may supply an id, but every explicit write must take it from the column's own sequence or run setval(pg_get_serial_sequence('nexus.catalog_collections','collection_id'), max) afterwards. (2) UNIQUE (tenant_id, collection_id) and UNIQUE (tenant_id, collection_id, embedding_model), the targets of P3.3a's id-twin foreign keys and of the RDR-225 composite's future key. No lock_timeout on the ALTER: the boot is not serving. DATA EFFECT: rewrites nexus.catalog_collections once (it holds the registry, the only user-data table this stage touches, by ruling); no row of any other table is read or written.

preConditions.sqlCheck: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_class WHERE oid = to_regclass('nexus.aspect_extraction_queue') AND NOT pg_has_role(current_user, relowner, 'USAGE')

changeSet.comment: nexus.aspect_extraction_queue (retired by aspects-005; kept only on a store whose queue held rows): collection_id bigint and aspect_extraction_queue_collection_id_check, NOT VALID. Guarded the way aspects-005-1 is: when to_regclass('nexus.aspect_extraction_queue') is NULL (a fresh install, and almost every other) the changeset does nothing and is recorded as run; the rollback is guarded the same way. It is its own changeset so no other table's changeset needs the table to exist (RDR-229 residual R3). lock_timeout stays on the ADD COLUMN. A precondition with onFail="CONTINUE" onError="CONTINUE", as aspects-005-2, skips the changeset when the table exists and the migration role does not own it (the ALTER would raise, and a boot must not halt: the no-wedge directive): nothing is recorded and the next boot retries it. An absent table passes the precondition (the DO guard then does nothing and the changeset is recorded), so a fresh install never retries. DATA EFFECT: none; a nullable ADD COLUMN and a NOT VALID constraint touch no row.

changeSet.author: nexus-p2m1x.17

preConditions.sqlCheck: SELECT count(*) FROM nexus.catalog_collections c WHERE c.superseded_by <> '' AND c.superseded_by_id IS NULL AND c.model_version = ''

changeSet.comment: catalog_collections_superseded_by_id_check, (superseded_by = '') = (superseded_by_id IS NULL), NOT VALID: it holds for every new or updated row, and is then VALIDATED IN THIS CHANGESET WHEN NO ROW VIOLATES IT (below), else by the stamp move's on_complete. THE 068-2 DATA PRECONDITION (linda's ruling 2026-11-21, item e): a NOT VALID CHECK refuses an UPDATE of an unstamped tombstone row with 23514, and D2's repair-catalog-collection-model-version move UPDATEs exactly the tombstones with a blank model_version, so on a skip-upgrade install (from before 0.1.200 straight to the Phase 3 release) the CHECK must not land while any registry row has superseded_by <> '' AND superseded_by_id IS NULL AND model_version = ''. This changeset waits (onFail="CONTINUE": skipped, nothing recorded, retried every boot) on that DATA and not on D2's state: a precondition naming D2's label would skip the CHECK forever if D2 failed permanently (M1). The wait ends when D2 completes or when P3.1's own superseded_by stamp fills superseded_by_id, so the CHECK lands after the stamp at the latest. Only this CHECK waits: the column (vectors-068-2), the other Expand CHECKs and the dual write go ahead. It is its own changeset, after the column's, because Liquibase skips a whole changeset: a precondition on the changeset that adds the column would leave an install with such a tombstone without superseded_by_id, and the dual write would then fail with 42703. onError="CONTINUE" keeps a boot from halting on the check itself (the no-wedge directive); the engine's completion check refuses the switch while this CHECK is missing and nx doctor names the waiting count. The precondition reads the registry through the migrating role's owner-read policy (catalog_collections_owner_read, D2's vectors-065, which owns it): the registry is FORCE row-secured, so this changeset depends on 065 BY INCLUDE ORDER, and the include of this file must come after vectors-065 (this tree does not carry 065; the next sync with develop supplies it). Where the migrating role is the serving role, that policy is skipped and D2's move is blocked too, so no UPDATE can meet the CHECK. The count is a read; the body names only catalog_collections (an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE ALTER on that one table, nothing in the chunk family). Guarded by tests/test_p31_superseded_by_check_precondition_lint.py. THE VALIDATE (seam 2, 2026-11-21): on a skip-upgrade install the precondition holds this changeset back until the stamp has filled superseded_by_id, so it lands on a LATER boot, after the registry stamp move has completed and its on_complete has run; nothing would ever validate the CHECK then, and the completion check's gate 1 (complete only while the CHECKs are present and validated) could never hold. So the changeset validates the CHECK itself, in the DO block after the ADD, but only when no row violates it: the precondition counts only the blank-model_version tombstones, so on an ordinary upgrade a tombstone with a model_version and no superseded_by_id is still unstamped when this runs, and a VALIDATE then would raise 23514 and halt the boot. The stamp move's on_complete validates it in that case (it validates only if the constraint exists, as before). LOCKS: the ADD takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on nexus.catalog_collections and the VALIDATE (SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE) scans it while the changeset's transaction still holds the first; the registry is small (171 rows on nexus, 42 on gate-xr789 at the P3.2 census), so the hold is milliseconds, and the boot is not serving. No lock_timeout, as in vectors-068-1. DATA EFFECT: none; no user-data row is written (a VALIDATE writes pg_constraint only). THE SINGLE-ROLE POSTURE (fix round A, critique B3): where the migrating role is nexus_svc, or inherits it, vectors-065 skips catalog_collections_owner_read (RDR-246, a supported BYO posture), the registry is FORCE row-secured, and this changeset's reads see ZERO rows (the tenant GUC is unset). The guard above is then vacuously true while the VALIDATE scans every row whatever the policies say, so it raised 23514 on any pre-P3.1 tombstone (every install that ever renamed a collection), the changeset rolled back and the engine did not start, every boot. So the VALIDATE never fails the changeset: it is wrapped in BEGIN ... EXCEPTION WHEN check_violation THEN NULL, and the CHECK stays NOT VALID for the stamp's on_complete. The precondition above is blind in that posture too (it counts no tombstone). THIS CHANGESET DELIBERATELY TREATS "CANNOT SEE" AS "CLEAN" and lets the CHECK land NOT VALID: in that posture D2's repair move and every stamp move are blocked by the row-security refusal in MovePreflight (the migrating role cannot read every tenant's rows of their driving table), so no UPDATE can meet the CHECK, and a NOT VALID CHECK is what the dual write needs from the first write. Skipping the CHECK instead would leave gate 1 unable to hold in a posture where the moves cannot run anyway and give the dual write nothing to enforce. The residue: a DBA who later adds an owner-read policy by hand lets D2's move run, and a blank-model_version tombstone then fails its UPDATE with 23514 until its superseded_by_id is stamped; the completion check's checks_missing and nx doctor name the wait.

rollback.sql: ALTER TABLE nexus.catalog_collections DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS catalog_collections_superseded_by_id_check;
